applicationFacts: The main API returns parsed response data; its raw method returns the Fetch response with parsed data stored in _data.
The client supports configurable defaults and creates derived clients with merged options.
JSON-compatible request bodies on payload methods are serialized and receive default JSON Content-Type and Accept headers when those headers are not already set.
Response parsing can be selected explicitly or inferred from Content-Type; the implementation supports JSON, text, blob, array buffer, and stream responses.
HTTP responses with status codes from 400 through 599 are treated as errors unless ignoreResponseError is enabled.
Retries can be configured by count, status-code list, and delay; by default, payload methods receive no retry and other methods receive one retry.
The client supports lifecycle hooks for request, request error, response, and response error events.
The Node.js entry point uses global Fetch APIs when available and otherwise provides a node-fetch-native fallback.
